not_found: Isotope shifts of the stable pair 76-72 and of lines other than 269.13 nm: Wang et al. measured only A = 68-74; Heilig, Riesner, Steudel, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 56, 1406 (1966) could not be opened (publisher access only)

Absolute (frequency-comb or wavemeter-traceable) transition frequencies of Ge I: none located; the best wavelengths remain the interferometric ones of Andrew and Meissner (1959) / Kaufman and Andrew, already behind the NIST levels
Hyperfine constants of 73Ge in excited levels other than 4p5s 3P°1: none located
Measured Lande g factors of the odd levels (Andrew, Cowan, Giacchetti, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 57, 715 (1967)): paper not accessible; the NIST levels file already carries its g values (Lande column)

Measured lifetimes or forbidden-line A values of the metastable 4p2 3P1, 3P2, 1D2, 1S0 levels: no measurement located; Garstang (1964) theory given instead. The newer calculation of Biemont and Hansen, Phys. Scr. 33, 117 (1986) could not be opened

Tint, Kono, Goto (1990), Andersen et al. (1975), Lotrian et al. (1978), Kessler et al. (2007): originals not accessible (publisher bot walls); their numbers appear here only as quoted by Li et al. / Biemont et al. / NIST

The web-search tool was unavailable in this session (search budget exhausted), so sources were located only by following NIST bibliography entries, DOIs and reference lists; a newer measurement that is not in the NIST bibliographic databases could have been missed
conflicts: 4p5s lifetimes: laser values of Biemont et al. 1999 (4.81, 4.68, 4.50, 4.23 ns) agree with Tint et al. 1990 (delayed coincidence) within errors; beam-foil values of Andersen et al. 1975 are 10-25 % shorter; Komarovskii and Verolainen 1989 are 30-65 % longer (judged systematic by Biemont et al.)

NIST ASD A values (Wiese and Martin 1980, accuracy C) versus the laser-lifetime x branching-ratio values kept here: e.g. 271.0 nm 2.8e8 vs 2.08(6)e8 s^-1, 265.2 nm (3P2-3P°2) 2.0e8 vs 1.60(7)e8, 303.9 nm 2.8e8 vs 2.04(5)e8, 468.6 nm 9.5e6 vs 4.98(54)e5 s^-1 (factor 19), 422.7 nm 2.1e7 vs 9.43(98)e6; NIST values are systematically larger because they were normalised to the shorter beam-foil lifetimes

Li et al. 1999 Table III, line 4p2 1D2 - 4p4d 3D°2 (239.4 nm): printed BR 0.0200(30) is inconsistent with the printed A = 0.00328(54)e8 s^-1 and log gf = -2.85 by a factor of 10; A as printed is kept, BR is flagged
4p4d 3D°1 (48962.78 cm^-1): the branch to 4p2 3P2 at 210.23 nm has BR 0.0040(4), the 800.1 nm infrared branch could not be detected and was neglected by Li et al. in the branching fractions
4p4d lifetimes: Li et al. 1999 (laser) vs Tint et al. 1990: agreement within errors except 3F°2 13.1(5) vs 15.2(8) ns and 3D°2 6.1(4) vs 6.9(3) ns
notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/Ge_I_levels.tsv); Li et al. and Biemont et al. quote the same levels rounded to 0.01 cm^-1. A_s of E1 lines = measured branching ratio x 1/(measured laser lifetime) as printed by the authors; rme_J_ea0 is derived from that A with the NIST energies (convention of SCHEMA.md, J' = upper level). 4p5s lifetimes and 4p2-4p5s A values come from Biemont et al. 1999 (read directly; Li et al. 1999 reprints them), 4p4d / 4p6s / 4p5d lifetimes and 4p2-4p4d A values from Li et al. 1999. Forbidden-line rates and the metastable lifetimes derived from them are 1964 intermediate-coupling THEORY (Garstang), not measurements. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second), centre of gravity, natural reference isotope 72Ge. Hyperfine constants refer to 73Ge (I = 9/2). Deverall, Meissner, Zissis, Phys. Rev. 95, 1463 (1954) (abstract) report no resolvable structure in eight Ge I lines and estimate the shift between consecutive even isotopes as smaller than 0.005 cm^-1 (bound).
